blocks.heading: Science, Merchant Navy, Pilot Training, and NDA

items.text: These four routes rarely appear in a standard "courses after 12th" list, but each one is a real, structured career with its own entrance entry requirement.
IMU CET requires at least 60% marks in PCM together at Class 12 and 50% in English, with age limits that vary by category.

blocks.heading: Worth Adding on Top of Any Degree

items.text: Whichever course from the list above you choose, the real advantage comes from what you add on top of it, not from the degree title alone.
Coursera and edX for a formal sequence

The Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate on Coursera is a genuinely useful, currently active option for building spreadsheet, SQL, and visualization skills alongside a BSc or BTech, and Harvard's CS50 on edX remains one of the strongest free foundations in programming logic before you specialize.
The four questions is the simplest way to compare two courses from this list without relying on gut feeling or family pressure alone.
Ask what your actual daily work would look like in each course's eventual career, screens and code, labs and circuits, ships and machinery, numbers and risk models, or a cockpit.
A PCM student who dislikes long isolated study should think twice before a pure-research BS-MS, no matter how prestigious the IISER brand sounds.

blocks.heading: Coaching Culture Around JEE and NEET Crowds

items.text: Actuarial science, Merchant Navy, and integrated science routes rarely get mentioned in school career talks.
Families hear "BSc" and assume it is automatically the weaker choice, without checking what the specific BSc leads to.
Nobody explains which entrance exam actually opens which door, so students prepare for one exam and never hear about six others.
You want a tech career but do not want, or cannot afford, a 4-year BTech.
You are comfortable building your own project portfolio instead of leaning on a college brand.
You may want to add an MCA or a specialised certification later for a stronger ceiling.
Your family budget genuinely cannot stretch to a 4-year BTech at a college that adds real value.
You already know you want a research, teaching, or MSc route after graduation.
